stack.clientTransport: plain HTTP on loopback with X-Forwarded-Proto: https from a trusted proxy address; TLS termination and reverse-proxy cost are excluded
stack.authentication: bearer API tokens; one runner principal per admission slice, the workspace owner for reads
stack.workers: A real worker (Docker executor) runs three Runs to publish the artifacts that are read, then is stopped. During measurement its worker row is kept ready by a benchmark heartbeat because admission is refused without a live worker; no process claims work, so admitted Runs stay queued and the benchmark measures the control plane only
stack.cache: warm: five unmeasured requests per operation precede each series; the first of them is reported as coldFirstRequestMs
stack.network: loopback only; target is a local node:http fixture, no external network

dataset.seededRunShape: terminal Run documents built by RunsService.prepare (admission snapshot included) and completed; no attempts, steps, events or artifacts

method.load: closed loop: each worker issues its next request as soon as the previous finishes; no think time
method.referenceSeriesSource: specs/10-validation.md 9 (concurrency series 1/4/8); the other levels are reported as stress levels and do not decide a verdict
method.percentileRule: p95 is reported as a measurement from 100 successful samples, p99 from 500; below that the number is shown but flagged unsupported and never decides a verdict
method.errorHandling: failed or non-expected-status requests are counted as errors and excluded from latency percentiles; a level with errors cannot be 'met'

fixtureTargetRequests.note: The target is only hit while the three artifact Runs execute; admission, listing, SSE and artifact reads send it nothing, so controller, queue and storage load is separate from target load

limitations: Single host: server, PostgreSQL container and the load generator share one machine and its other workloads (see loadAverage).
Every PostgreSQL write transaction takes one advisory lock (ADR-015), so writes are serialized; the synchronous bridge blocks the server's only JavaScript thread for each query.
Latencies are API request times, not UI render times; the UI targets are mapped to their API analogues.
Orchestration overhead, queue start lag and artifact publication need executed Runs under load and are not measured.
Artifacts are small (a few KiB); throughput for large artifacts is not measured.
Distributed scale, S3-compatible storage and distributed SLOs belong to M5; Windows and macOS to M6.
